html:
The 2011 uprising in Bahrain was a wave of mass protest that began on 14 February 2011 at the Pearl Roundabout in Manama, part of the Arab Spring.

Protesters, mostly from the Shia majority, asked for an elected government and an end to discrimination. In March troops from Saudi Arabia and the UAE crossed the causeway to back the government, a state of emergency was declared, and the camp was cleared by force. The monument at the roundabout was pulled down.

Opposition parties were later banned and many leaders jailed. The uprising showed how closely the Al Khalifa depend on their Gulf neighbours.
sum: The 2011 uprising in Bahrain was a wave of mass protest that began on 14 February 2011 at the Pearl Roundabout in Manama, part of the Arab Spring.
